children: OTTAWA--Factory activity in Canada recovered last month, with an early estimate pointing to a rebound in sales following the first drop in six months.
Manufacturing shipments rose an estimated 1.1% in August from a month prior, Statistics Canada said Thursday.
The largest increases were in sales of primary metals and chemicals, the agency said.

The rise follows a 0.4% fall in manufacturing sales in July, due to weakness in chemicals and a retreat in food manufacturing, though compared with a year earlier sales were 10.9% higher. In volume terms, sales in July were down 1.4% for the month and up a modest 0.4% on a year prior.

The Statistics Canada's sales projection for August was based on a weighted response rate to its monthly survey of roughly 74%. The official survey results, based on more complete data, are scheduled to be released Oct. 15 .

S&P Global's latest Canada manufacturing purchasing managers index continues to signal an industry that is growing, albeit with activity cooling modestly and input price inflation remaining elevated in August. The index slipped to 53 from 53.5 the month before, a fifth straight month above the 50 threshold between growth and decline.

Manufacturing in Canada has recovered this year as companies have adapted to the shift in U.S. trade policy and President Trump's tariffs, though uncertainty is again high after relations between Washington and Ottawa recently deteriorated and as fuel prices remain elevated.
